messages:
sam: heads up — canary rollout for model-infer v1.3 in us-west is showing 4x 95p latency and ~20% 5xxs. dashboard for the canary panels are blank in console, so it's hard to see root cause. starting a thread.
incident-bot: INC-2112345678 created. Pager notified: @sre-oncall.
sre-oncall: I’m on it. Maya, can you pull traces? Liz, can you check traffic split + feature-flag status for model_canary?
maya: looking now. quick note — X-Ray traces for that cluster are missing from the last deploy window. agent logs show startup errors.
liz: checking ff service — attempting toggle now. last toggle call returned 500 a few minutes ago.
liz: toggling ff off for canary traffic:
```
curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/toggle -d '{"flag":"model_canary","state":"off"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx"
```
raj: preparing rollback in case kill-switch doesn't stick. will try `kubectl rollout undo` for the canary deployment.
raj: running:
```
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/model-infer-canary --to-revision=3
```
deploy-bot: rollback started for deployment/model-infer-canary (initiated by raj).
sre-oncall: confirmed the FLAG endpoint returned 500 because the ff-worker crashed on the new image — so the kill-switch didn't propagate. good catch.
sam: customer impact? do we have counts on failed requests / affected orgs?
sre-oncall: 12 distinct customers saw 5xxs in the last 10m, error rate delta +0.8% overall. severity: medium but noisy. sending status to support.
caroline: messaged support w/ short blurb and current mitigation steps. cc-ing CS.
alex: grafana dashboards were empty because the grafana configmap got overwritten by the deploy (datasource reference changed). I reverted the configmap and restarted grafana pod. dashboards back. :relieved:
maya: trace agent fix — env var for TRACE_ENDPOINT was pointing to old host due to helm values mismatch. I patched the daemonset with correct env. traces should appear in ~30s.
sre-oncall: alerts are noisy: alertmanager has both canary and prod latency rules firing; need to silence canary alerts while we triage (so SREs don't page while rollback finishes).
liz: creating a silence scoped to canary alerts for 1h:
```
POST /api/v2/silences
{ "matchers": [{"name":"deployment","value":"model-infer-canary","isRegex":false}], "startsAt": "2026-03-15T01:00:00Z", "endsAt": "2026-03-15T02:00:00Z", "createdBy": "liz", "comment": "silence canary alerts during rollback" }
```
sre-oncall: silence created. routing rules adjusted so production pages still land but reduced duplicate noise.
raj: canary rollback completed and verified — pods back to stable revision, traffic split set to 0% canary.
liz: feature flag forcibly set to off (manual override) and ff-worker restarted to prevent accidental re-enable.
sam: do we have a timeline for why kill-switch failed? sounds like two root causes: ff-worker crash + grafana/helm config drift hiding telemetry.
maya: yep — initial deploy changed helm values for both the flag-worker and grafana datasource. the flag-worker crash prevented kill API; grafana change hid the canary metrics which delayed detection.
alex: I've pinned grafana values in the chart to avoid implicit overwrite and opened a PR to add a preflight check.
sre-oncall: mitigation summary: 1) rollback complete; 2) feature flag off; 3) grafana reverted; 4) tracing agent patched; 5) silence created for canary alerts; 6) support notified.
sam: handoff — liz will own post-incident follow-up (postmortem + action items) tomorrow morning. liz, please own backlog.
liz: ACK. I’ll gather deploy diffs, helm value changes, and correlate with the infra commits.
caroline: support confirmed limited customer impact; no escalations. Sending customer-facing note in 30m.
raj: q: do we want an automated preflight that verifies kill-switch endpoint after a deploy? seems critical.
alex: +1. propose we add a post-deploy healthcheck job that hits ff endpoints and key telemetry (grafana datasource, trace producer). will sketch a RFC.
sre-oncall: reopening alerting rule to be canary-only badge + add a guard so we only page on prod threshold breach.
incident-bot: INC-2112345678 resolved at 2112347900. Postmortem required: assign to liz, severity: SEV-2, timeline recorded.
sam: thanks everyone — good quick coordination. follow-ups in #postmortems. :thumbsup:
